title: QBR Token Capacity & Runway Checklist
content:
Purpose: Lightweight QBR worksheet to quickly diagnose token consumption trends, rate-limit impacts, and budget runway; produce clear ask and next steps for renewal conversations.

How to use: Fill in the shaded inputs (Customer placeholders) before the call. Use the heatmap + anomaly checklist to prioritize follow-ups. This is intentionally compact for slide -> talking points.

1) Executive snapshot (one-line)
- Current 30d token spend: {{30d_tokens}} tokens (${{30d_cost}})
- Average RPS: {{avg_rps}}; 99th p99 latency target met: YES/NO
- Active routes: {{top_3_routes}}
- Billing tier / committed spend: {{commit_tier}}

2) Key metrics (fill for 30 / 90 / 365 windows)
- Total tokens consumed
- Billable tokens (exclude cached hits)
- Requests per second (avg / peak)
- Failed requests / throttles (count and % of total)
- Cache hit rate (prefix/KV)
- Cost per 1k tokens (effective, after credits)

3) Token burn heatmap (quick ascii visualization to bring to QBR)
- Week 1: |||| ||| ||   (low)
- Week 2: ||||||||||||   (spike)
- Week 3: |||| ||||  (medium)
- Week 4: ||||| ||    (decline)
Notes: call out any >50% week-to-week increases and correlate to release/feature names.

4) Rate-limit impact matrix (triage table)
- Symptom: repeated 429s on route X -> Likely cause: client burst > allowed RPS; Mitigation: suggest queueing/backoff and short-term burst allowance policy (proposal: +25% for 2 weeks).
- Symptom: tail latency increase -> Likely cause: large batch windows; Mitigation: reduce max tokens per request or switch to pre-warming slot.

5) Budget alert playbook (if daily spend > budget threshold):
- Auto actions: send alert to customer billing alias + CS lead; throttle non-critical routes by 30%; enable fallback to quantized cheaper model for non-production routes.
- Manual actions: offer 14-day emergency top-up or short-term committed runway at negotiated rate.
- Messaging template (short): "Heads up — your 7d spend is pacing X% above the agreed run rate. We can enable temporary burst capacity + cheaper model routing; want me to open that?"

6) Renewal / runway score (quick formula, 0-100 where higher = healthy)
- Score components (weights): usage stability 40%, budget adherence 30%, SLA incidents 20%, adoption signals 10%
- Quick calc: stability (0-40) + adherence (0-30) + incidents (0-20) + adoption (0-10) = total
- Red flags: score < 55 -> escalate to AM + Solutions Eng

7) QBR script / talking points (5 min ops + 10 min commercial)
- Ops: "We observed X% token growth this quarter driven by feature Y. We recommend A/B migration to smaller context windows for route Z and enabling prefix caching where possible."
- Commercial: "Based on runway projections, you will breach your committed tier in T weeks. Options: increase commit, add burst allowance, or enable autoscaling for critical routes."

8) Action items & owners (example rows)
- [ ] Confirm top-3 heavy prompts and mark for optimization — Owner: Solutions Eng (Miguel) — Due: 2 weeks
- [ ] Enable daily spend alert at ${{daily_alert_threshold}} — Owner: CS Ops (Aisha) — Due: 48 hours
- [ ] Proposal: 30-day emergency runway (cost + terms) — Owner: AM (Priya) — Due: 3 business days

9) Notes to self / open questions to bring to customer
- Which routes are non-critical and safe to throttle?
- Any upcoming marketing/events that could cause spikes?
- Are embedding / vector indexing jobs scheduled at off-peak windows?

10) Appendix: quick diagnostic commands and links
- Pull 7d token delta: report id CONFLUENCE-5821 or run internal query: analytics.tokens.delta(customer_id, 7)
- Rate-limit logs: see Kibana dashboard: kbn.redwood/rate-limits/{{customer_id}}
- Escalation path: CS -> Solutions Eng -> On-call Infra (pager)

Draft checklist complete; copy into QBR slide as "Usage & Billing snapshot" and attach the three recommended mitigations. Replace placeholders before meeting.

Version notes: created by Aisha Patel (CS Ops) — working draft for internal review.
